Design system

Component gallery

Every specimen the generator writes, on one page. This gallery links ../static/app.css instead of inlining it, so editing a token and reloading shows the change with no rebuild. The standalone card beside each specimen is the opposite trade: it inlines the stylesheet, so it is a frozen copy that renders anywhere on its own. Sections are the stylesheet's own twelve, read out of it at build time.

1. RESET

app.css lines 23–86 · no specimen

Normalisation only. It carries no specimen because every specimen below is already standing on it.

2. TOKENS - LIGHT

app.css lines 87–313 · 5 specimens

The light palette and every non-colour scale: type, weight, spacing, radius, elevation and the two font stacks. The five foundation specimens read from here.

Colour tokens

cards/foundations-colour.html

Colour system

Both themes are authored independently. Dark is the working default for long analysis sessions; light is tuned for print and projection rather than derived by inverting the dark ramp. Every component reads only from these names, so a theme change is a token swap and nothing else.

Monospace stack

cards/foundations-monospace.html

Monospace stack

All byte data uses "Cascadia Mono", "Cascadia Code", Consolas, "Segoe UI Mono", monospace with ligatures and contextual alternates disabled, so != never fuses and every column is exactly one advance wide. Numerals are tabular throughout.

app.css lines 723–1264 · 6 specimens

The chrome around the editor, from the menu bar down to the status bar.

Application shell

cards/chrome-app-shell.html

Application shell

The whole chrome composed at once: menu bar, toolbar, document tabs, the editor, a right dock and a bottom dock either side of their splitters, and the status bar. The shell is a five row grid whose editor row is minmax(0, 1fr), so the docks hold their size and only the editor absorbs the remaining height.

Dock tabs

Splitters are 5px hit targets that stay invisible until hovered, then reveal a short grip and an accent wash.

Status bar

Every reading is a labelled monospace pair, so values stay aligned as they change under the caret. Severity is carried by the state dot as well as by colour.

7. HEX EDITOR

app.css lines 1265–1792 · 4 specimens

The hex view itself: the ruler, the offset gutter, the row, and the composable state slots on a single byte cell.

Byte cell states

cards/editor-byte-states.html

Byte class tinting

Class tinting is the lowest layer. It colours the glyph and adds a barely-there wash, so structure is visible without competing with any editing state drawn on top of it.

Four classes
00null0x00
41printable0x20 to 0x7E
0Dcontrolbelow 0x20, and 0x7F
C3high0x80 to 0xFF

States

Each state writes into its own custom-property slot on the cell, so the layers composite instead of overwriting one another.

Single states
4Dnormalno state
4Dselectedinside the active selection
4Dselected, unfocusedselection while another pane has focus
4Dcaretcaret cell, whole byte
4Dnibble caret, highediting the high nibble
4Dnibble caret, lowediting the low nibble
4Dcaret, unfocusedcaret position with focus elsewhere
4Dmodifiedunsaved edit
4Dbookmarkedcorner flag plus ring
4Dsearch hit, first byteleading edge bar
4Dsearch hitinside a match
4Dtemplate field, startleft cap of a field run
4Dtemplate fieldinside a field run
4Dtemplate field, endright cap of a field run
4Ddiff addedpresent only in B
4Ddiff removedpresent only in A
4Ddiff modifieddiffers between A and B

Composition

Region backgrounds blend, edge markers occupy different edges, and the caret is drawn last with a contrast ring so it survives every combination.

Combined states
5Aselected + modifiedlayered slots stay legible
5Aselected + search hitlayered slots stay legible
5Aselected + modified + hitlayered slots stay legible
5Acaret + selected + modifiedlayered slots stay legible
5Anibble caret + selected + hitlayered slots stay legible
5Abookmarked + field startlayered slots stay legible
5Abookmarked + selected + modifiedlayered slots stay legible
5Adiff + hit + selectedlayered slots stay legible
5Acaret over three region stateslayered slots stay legible

Sample view

cards/editor-sample-view.html

Forty rows against a real PE header

The sample is the first 640 bytes of a 64-bit PE image: DOS header, DOS stub, Rich header, the PE signature at 0x0F0, the COFF and optional headers, and the start of the section table. A selection, a nibble caret, a bookmark, modified bytes, three template fields, three search hits and two diff regions are all live at once.

Busy hatch

cards/editor-busy.html

Busy hatch

A mutating operation covers the affected view with a drifting diagonal hatch rather than an opaque spinner overlay, so the underlying data stays readable while it is known to be stale. The drift stops under reduced motion.

transform_data

Stale panel

hb-hatch is the same texture without the overlay positioning, applied directly to any surface whose contents are known to be out of date. Here it sits on a padded panel body rather than an absolutely placed layer.

Panel awaiting recompute
Entropyentropy_map(window=256)

The document changed under this reading. The panel keeps the previous curve legible beneath the hatch instead of blanking, because a stale answer is more useful than none while the recompute runs.

Re-sorted and de-emphasised

Clicking a second header moves the sort caret and flips it to is-sort-desc. Rows that survive the query but fall under the current display cutoff stay in place as is-muted rather than vanishing, so the count in the footer keeps matching what the engine returned.

Truncation banner

The transport caps inline payloads at 4096 bytes but always reports the true length, so the banner can state exactly how much was elided and offer the window endpoint instead of silently showing less.

10. ANALYSIS

app.css lines 3163–3379 · 6 specimens

The analysis figures. The application paints these into a canvas; the specimens draw the same geometry as SVG so the gallery stays static.

Entropy strip

cards/analysis-entropy.html

Entropy strip

Shannon entropy over 256 byte windows, 64 readings across the 16 KiB analysis buffer, computed here rather than asserted. The curve tracks the header, the code section, the string table, a run of alignment padding and a packed region; the dashed rule marks the 7.0 bit threshold above which the engine calls a block high entropy.

Entropywindow 256 B · 64 points · peak 7.30
0x00000000 to 0x00003FFF · y axis 0.0 to 8.0 bits per byte
0x000000000x000020000x00003FFF

Content classification

cards/analysis-classification.html

Content classification

content_classification(256) returns one code per block, and all five codes occur in this buffer. Every legend entry carries its numeric code as well as its colour, so the strip stays readable without colour discrimination and survives greyscale printing.

Classificationblock 256 B · 64 blocks · 5 classes
0x00000000 to 0x00003FFF · one column per block
0x00000000block size 256 B0x00003FFF
0Zero filledevery byte 0x001Plaintext-likeprintable, low entropy2Moderatestructured binary3High entropyH > 7.0, packed or encrypted4MixedH 4.5 to 7.0, code or tables

Selection marker

The strip is the link back to the editor rather than a separate report: whatever is selected in the document is drawn over it as a translucent overlay, so the 3072 bytes under the caret can be located in the whole buffer at a glance. The overlay uses the same selection fill and border as the editor, and never occludes the classes beneath it.

Selection0x00002800 · 3072 B
the overlay carries the editor selection fill and border · the classes stay visible beneath it
0x00000000selection 0x00002800 to 0x000033FF0x00003FFF

Digram matrix

cards/analysis-digram.html

Digram matrix

digram_matrix() returns exactly 65536 counts, row-major at idx = b0 * 256 + b1. The dense band is the ASCII string table and the scatter is the packed region. The frame here is the reusable canvas chrome; the application paints the same figure into a real canvas element at this size.

Digram5393 distinct pairs · peak 1727
x axis first byte 0x00 to 0xFF · y axis second byte · opacity by count
